solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Messy pig or neat butterfly

indicators.note: something messy is jumbled up, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A contrast between a slovenly pig and something tidy, or a dainty insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messy' rearranges PIGORNEAT, all nine letters of 'pig or neat', the 'or' included.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a common European species of white butterfly whose males have orange wingtips.

clue.text: Volunteer no longer a royalist?

parts.note: something no longer on is off, as a cancelled event is off
a royalist supports ER, the Queen (Elizabeth Regina); a royalist no longer is off ER

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped supporting the monarchy steps forward to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: one who is off ER, the Queen, is no longer a royalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward without being asked, a synonym of making an offer.

clue.text: Next to do a single turn

indicators.note: a turn here is a change of order, so the letters of the three words are reshuffled

explanation.surface: An instruction for a dance or drill: beside your partner, perform one twirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges DOASINGLE, the nine letters of 'do a single'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alongside something means being beside it, a direct synonym of being next to it.

clue.text: Successful player ends run around centre

indicators.note: around says the first pieces are placed on either side of the next one

parts.note: in football the two ends of the pitch are the goals
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
the core of something is its centre

explanation.surface: A winning sportsman finishes a lap circling the middle of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' looks like 'finishes' but means the goals at each end of a football pitch; 'around' wraps the first two pieces about the centre piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer who puts the ball in the net is a successful attacking player, the scorer of goals.

clue.text: Bit of mosaic Greek god put up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, so the whole run is backwards

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
to put something down is to set it

explanation.surface: A fragment of mosaic showing an Olympian deity has been installed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ARESSET round as one run, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles or pieces of glass from which a mosaic is assembled.

clue.text: Claim made by old female in Fleet Street

indicators.note: in says the two letters are placed inside the newspaper word

parts.note: Fleet Street in London was the home of the British national newspapers, so it stands for the press

explanation.surface: An allegation made by an elderly woman, reported by the national newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is the London street long synonymous with British newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To profess something is to declare or assert it, often falsely, which is what claiming does.

clue.text: Be in time to see a fly in the ointment

definitions.meaning: to arrive in time to see a show or a train is to manage not to miss it
a hidden snag or drawback in an otherwise good thing

explanation.definitionFit: One catches a film or a bus by getting there in time, and a hidden snag in a deal is a catch.

clue.text: Audible place name

indicators.note: audible means heard, so a word is replaced by another sounding the same

parts.note: a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: A place name you can hear spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite someone is to mention or quote them by name, a verb synonym of naming.

clue.text: Indian agent finally raised capital

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows
in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: Lima is the capital city of Peru

explanation.surface: An Indian spy at last brought up some money for investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LIMA into AMIL; 'capital' looks financial but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka, so a Tamil is an Indian.

clue.text: Hot Paris cop ordered spiced wine

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French policeman on a hot day asked for a mulled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges PARISCOP into IPPOCRAS; it poses as the ordering of a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocras is a medieval drink of wine sweetened and flavoured with spices such as cinnamon.

clue.text: A girl growing things

definitions.meaning: a woman's given name, also that of the Roman goddess of flowers
the plant life of a region, everything that grows there

explanation.definitionFit: Flora is a girl's name and also the collective term for the plants of an area.

clue.text: Violent film brought back to Australian native in store

indicators.note: in says these pieces go inside the word for a store

parts.note: a store is a shop

indicators.note: brought back means the small word is turned round

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird native to Australia

explanation.surface: An action movie was returned to an Aussie at the shop where it was hired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses only the little word 'to'; 'native' suggests a person but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-'em-up is a film or video game consisting mostly of gunfights and violent action.

clue.text: Put on record that's made an impression

definitions.meaning: entered formally in an official list
had an effect, got noticed, as in a remark that ... with them

explanation.definitionFit: A registered letter is officially recorded, and an idea that registered was taken in or noticed.

clue.text: Singer taking part in recital tonight

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A vocalist is performing in this evening's concert.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range just below soprano, so the word names a type of singer.

clue.text: Fruit, including fine European, British, American fruit

indicators.note: including means the other pieces go inside the fruit word

parts.note: a cherry is a fruit
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A list of produce from several countries, as on a shop label.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a list of fruit origins; 'including' opens the first fruit to take three short abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The chokeberry is a North American shrub of the rose family bearing small astringent berries.

clue.text: Sheep disheartened in Australia by a philosopher

indicators.note: losing its heart means the word loses everything but its outer letters

parts.note: Oz is a colloquial name for Australia

explanation.surface: A sheep farmer in the outback feels discouraged, but a thinker comes along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes HEE, the middle of SHEEP, leaving SP.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker, author of the Ethics.

clue.text: Was captain from Ostend regularly catching fish?

indicators.note: catching means the alternate letters close around the fish word
regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: A trawler skipper from the Belgian port often landed a haul.
explanation.walkthrough: Ostend is a Belgian port; 'regularly' takes its even letters, and 'catching' makes them close round the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To skipper a boat or team is to be its captain, so the past tense means was captain.

clue.text: Marchese dismissing a devious Machiavellian type

indicators.note: devious means twisted, so the remaining letters are rearranged
dismissing means one letter is sent away from the Italian title

explanation.surface: An Italian marquis sacks a crooked schemer from his court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' takes the A out of MARCHESE, leaving MRCHESE, which 'devious' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Machiavelli advocated cunning statecraft, so a Machiavellian type is a crafty plotter.

clue.text: ICBM for Tiny Tim?

definitions.meaning: a very small man, minute meaning tiny, Tim being a man's name

explanation.definitionFit: The Minuteman is a US nuclear missile, and a minute man is jokingly a tiny chap like Tiny Tim.

clue.text: Danger to shipping? Retired diver caught one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the bird is turned round

parts.note: a grebe is a diving waterbird

explanation.surface: A diver who has stopped working was arrested; a hazard to vessels lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns GREBE into EBERG; 'diver' is a bird, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Icebergs drift in shipping lanes and famously sank the Titanic, so they are a hazard at sea.

clue.text: Heavy water in part of India

indicators.note: in says the stream word goes inside the Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a rill is a small stream of water

explanation.surface: Dense, heavy water is found in a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy' is a noun: a thug or bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla, like a heavy, is slang for a big, intimidating thug or minder.

clue.text: Essential qualities needed for college graduate getting ahead

indicators.note: getting ahead means the graduate piece goes in front of the college piece

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate degree
King's is a college at Cambridge (and London)

explanation.surface: A career guide lists the qualities a young graduate needs to advance.
explanation.walkthrough: King's College is one of Cambridge University's colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: The makings of something are the qualities needed to develop into it, as in the makings of a star.

clue.text: Scottish island with one German plant

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A botanist visits a Hebridean island with a German friend to see the flora.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullein is a tall woolly-leaved plant of the figwort family with spikes of yellow flowers.

clue.text: Perform song on piano

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the song piece follows the piano letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Instructions to a musician to accompany a song at the keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To play music or a part is to perform it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Big hole in baby's shawl

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A large tear has appeared in the infant's wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, a very deep hole.

clue.text: Fossils discovered by lost tribe wandering around island

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the island letter
wandering means roving, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Explorers find relics left by a lost people roaming an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges LOSTTRIBE and 'around' puts I inside it, after TRILOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites were marine arthropods extinct for 250 million years, known only from fossil remains.

clue.text: Trim husband in bar

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as does save

explanation.surface: A man has his hair cut at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: To shave is to cut hair or a thin layer off closely, a synonym of trimming.

clue.text: Transport, we hear, for butcher

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like another word

parts.note: a sleigh is a sledge used to transport people over snow

explanation.surface: A butcher's van is overheard being mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to kill them brutally, and slay means to kill violently.

clue.text: Boys not happy in the shade

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Al is another boy's name
feeling blue means feeling sad, not happy

explanation.surface: Some lads are sulking, sitting out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shade' is a colour, not shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blue is a deep, vivid tone of blue, so it is a particular colour or hue.

clue.text: Steps taken for reform in Burma

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the letters of the country name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Measures were taken to bring political change to Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, and a dance is a sequence of steps.

clue.text: Simpson's first task outside Springfield

indicators.note: outside means the task word goes around the letter

parts.note: a duty is a task

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson's main job is out of his home town of Springfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Springfield poses as the Simpsons' town but is the singer Dusty Springfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty Springfield was a celebrated 1960s British pop singer, so her first name pairs with her surname.

clue.text: Pain anyone can suffer?

indicators.note: to suffer something is to be knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether pain is something everyone may feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffer' rearranges ANYONECAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain, as in a pain in the neck, is an irritation or nuisance.
